etymologies.etymologyHTML: From their general formula Cn(H2O)n; they were once thought to be hydrates of carbon.

definitions.definition: (organic chemistry, nutrition) A sugar, starch, or cellulose that is a food source of energy for an animal or plant.

quote.citation: 2013 September-October, Katie L. Burke, “In the News”, in American Scientist:
quote.text: Oxygen levels on Earth skyrocketed 2.4 billion years ago, when cyanobacteria evolved photosynthesis: the ability to convert water and carbon dioxide into carbohydrates and waste oxygen using solar energy.

definitions.definition: (colloquial, by extension, metonymically) Any food rich in starch or other carbohydrates.
